bdhs

bdhs is an R toolkit for every round of the Bangladesh Demographic and Health Survey: 1993-94, 1996-97, 1999-2000, 2004, 2007, 2011, 2014, 2017-18 and 2022. It also covers the Bangladesh Service Provision Assessments and the 2001 maternal mortality survey.

It does two jobs:

  1. Ships the official numbers. Every estimate the DHS Program publishes for Bangladesh (about 310,000 values: national, by division, by residence, wealth, education and more), with definitions, survey and dataset catalogues, cross-round codebooks, division crosswalks and maps. These work straight after installation, with no DHS account.
  2. Makes your own microdata painless. Once you have downloaded BDHS files from the DHS Program, bdhs registers them, reads any round in one line, harmonizes variables across rounds, builds the correct complex survey design, pools rounds, and computes indicators that are validated against the official DHS estimates.

Why isn’t the microdata included, like in brfss? BRFSS is US public domain data. DHS microdata are licensed to registered users, and the DHS terms of use say they “will not be re-distributed, either directly or within any tool”. bdhs respects that: it never bundles or uploads microdata. Registration is free and quick: https://dhsprogram.com/data/new-user-registration.cfm.

Installation 

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("armanhossen-am/bdhs")

Official estimates in one line 

library(bdhs)

bdhs_official("FE_FRTR_W_TFR")[, c("year_label", "indicator", "value")]
#> # A tibble: 9 × 3
#>   year_label indicator                  value
#>   <chr>      <chr>                      <dbl>
#> 1 1993-94    Total fertility rate 15-49   3.4
#> 2 1996-97    Total fertility rate 15-49   3.3
#> 3 1999-2000  Total fertility rate 15-49   3.3
#> 4 2004       Total fertility rate 15-49   3  
#> 5 2007       Total fertility rate 15-49   2.7
#> 6 2011       Total fertility rate 15-49   2.3
#> 7 2014       Total fertility rate 15-49   2.3
#> 8 2017-18    Total fertility rate 15-49   2.3
#> 9 2022       Total fertility rate 15-49   2.3
bdhs_plot_trend("CN_NUTS_C_HA2", by = "Residence")

bdhs_map("CN_NUTS_C_HA2", survey = 2022)

Not sure what an indicator or variable is called? Search everything at once:

bdhs_search("caesarean|cesarean")

Your microdata in one line 

# Once: register the files you downloaded (folders, zips, renamed files are fine)
bdhs_import("~/Downloads/BDHS")
bdhs_inventory()                       # what you have vs. what exists

ir <- bdhs_read(2022, "IR")            # women, 2022
kr <- bdhs_read("2017-18", "KR")       # children, 2017-18

bdhs_estimate(kr, c("rh_anc_4plus", "rh_del_facility", "rh_del_csection"),
              by = "v025")             # correct design, SEs, CIs
bdhs_validate(kr)                      # compare with official DHS values

# Big files: read only what some indicators need
ir <- bdhs_read(2022, "IR", indicators = c("fp_cpr_modern", "fp_unmet_total"))

bdhs_mortality(bdhs_read(2022, "BR"))  # NMR, IMR, U5MR with jackknife SEs

The same code runs on synthetic data from bdhs_simulate(), which has the structure of the real files with random values. That is how the examples, tests and vignettes run without real files:

kr <- bdhs_simulate(2022, "KR")
bdhs_estimate(kr, c("rh_anc_4plus", "rh_del_facility", "rh_del_csection"), by = "v025")
#> # BDHS estimates: 3 indicators | BD2022DHS | 95% CI
#> # A tibble: 6 × 11
#>   survey_id indicator     label v025  estimate    se ci_low ci_high n_unweighted
#>   <chr>     <chr>         <chr> <fct>    <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>        <int>
#> 1 BD2022DHS rh_anc_4plus  Four… urban     43.5  5.78   32.2    55.6           70
#> 2 BD2022DHS rh_anc_4plus  Four… rural     23.8  3.10   18.0    30.8           75
#> 3 BD2022DHS rh_del_facil… Deli… urban     59.4  7.93   42.6    74.2           78
#> 4 BD2022DHS rh_del_facil… Deli… rural     49.7  2.96   43.7    55.8           84
#> 5 BD2022DHS rh_del_csect… Deli… urban     29.2  6.66   17.5    44.5           78
#> 6 BD2022DHS rh_del_csect… Deli… rural     31.4  4.08   23.6    40.4           84
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: n_weighted <dbl>, api_id <chr>

What’s inside

Bundled data What it is
bdhs_indicators Every official DHS estimate for Bangladesh, all rounds and breakdowns
bdhs_indicator_catalog Definitions, denominators and coverage of each indicator
bdhs_surveys, bdhs_datasets Survey facts and the full list of 441 DHS data files
bdhs_codebook, bdhs_value_labels Variable names, labels and value labels across rounds (metadata only)
bdhs_regions Division codes per round with a cross-round crosswalk
bdhs_pool_population Female population 15-49 for pooled (de-normalized) weights
bdhs_boundaries() Division boundaries for each survey (DHS Spatial Data Repository)
Task Functions
Official estimates bdhs_official(), bdhs_plot_trend(), bdhs_map()
Discover bdhs_search(), bdhs_variable(), bdhs_describe()
Your files bdhs_import(), bdhs_read(), bdhs_inventory(), bdhs_download()
Cross-round work bdhs_harmonize(), bdhs_pool(), bdhs_merge(), bdhs_na()
Estimation bdhs_design(), bdhs_estimate(), bdhs_fertility(), bdhs_mortality(), bdhs_validate()
Teaching and testing bdhs_simulate()

Things bdhs handles for you

  • Ever-married samples. Every BDHS women’s sample is ever-married women, so “all women” indicators need the DHS all-woman factors (awfactt and friends). bdhs applies them where the DHS does.
  • Changing divisions. Bangladesh went from 5 divisions (1993-94) to 8 (2017-18 on), and the codes were renumbered when Mymensingh was created. bdhs maps every round onto consistent layouts.
  • Correct designs. Clusters, sampling-error strata and weights per round, lonely PSUs, and pooled multi-round designs.
  • DHS quirks. Special missing codes, flagged z-scores, 2-digit years in the early rounds, renamed and re-saved files, and recodes that only exist for some rounds.

Citation and conditions of use

Please cite bdhs and the data sources (citation("bdhs")). When you publish results from BDHS microdata, cite the survey’s final report. The DHS Program’s conditions for Bangladesh also ask you to send a copy of the publication to the NIPORT library.

bdhs is not affiliated with or endorsed by the DHS Program, ICF or NIPORT.
